title: Finite-cover connectedness criterion for abelian étale sections
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and i:Z→X a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume that for every finite morphism h:X′→X [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and every irreducible closed subset C⊆X′, C∩h⁻¹(range i) is connected and nonempty. Then for every abelian étale sheaf G on X [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], globalSectionsUpperStarMap Ab i G:Γ(X,G)→Γ(Z,i⁻¹G) is an isomorphism, with global sections and inverse image as in [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

source.place: Lemmas 59.82.4 (09ZG), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZG, and 59.82.2 (09ZF), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZF; underlying abelian sheaf version

proof.text: Finite covers of X are qcqs and spectral. Base change of i is closed, and its image is the inverse image of range i. Apply the spectral closed restriction criterion to each finite cover and its point closures; the hypothesis supplies connected nonempty intersections.

The identity is finite, so the previous step gives both comparisons required by Gabber’s Zariski-to-étale criterion. Apply that criterion to the underlying set sheaf of G to obtain bijective restriction.

Forgetting abelian groups preserves finite limits and filtered colimits. It commutes with the filtered pointwise inverse-image construction and sheafification. The comparisons respect adjunction units and terminal evaluation, identifying the underlying globalSectionsUpperStarMap with the bijection of the preceding step. Its inverse is additive, proving it an isomorphism.
